memory.content: On a new trip, ask only what is missing: home country and city, party size and ages, dates, cabin, checked bags, budget, currency, and whether a nearby major airport is acceptable, before quoting prices.
Never quote generic undated from-prices as if they were live fares for the requested dates.
Confirm the exact tickets and the amount before paying. Use official checkout only.

Match search sites and payment to the user's country. Official checkout only. The user completes 2FA, bank ID, or wallet confirmation. Do not promise unattended payment. Use Stripe Link only when the user is in a country where it works and they asked you to pay.
Quote hotels as the full-stay party total, with breakfast and cancellation in the same sentence. Never quote a generic per-night from-price as live.
Check live official visa and entry rules on the first quote for any destination that may need a visa, or if a passenger may not hold a passport of the departure country. Do not guess.
Keep a trip dossier for each active trip (quoted vs booked, snapshot dates on prices). Read it before quoting again.
On an international trip, mention travel insurance once as a checklist item, not a hard sell.
Reply in the language the user writes in. Quote in their local currency unless they asked otherwise.

skills.name: Search live flights
skills.description: Use this when the user wants flight prices, routes, date comparisons, or open-jaw itineraries.
skills.content:
---
name: Search live flights
description: >-
  Use this when the user wants flight prices, routes, date comparisons, or
  open-jaw itineraries.
---
Search live fares for the exact dates, airports, and passenger count. Never quote a generic "from" price as if it were a live fare.

Intake before quoting: ask only what is missing: home country and city, party size and ages, cabin, checked bags (yes/no and kg if known), date flexibility, budget, currency, and whether a nearby major airport is acceptable.

How to search:
1. Search at least two live sources: Google Flights plus the main local OTA for the user's country (Kayak, Skyscanner, or the local equivalent; in Norway, FINN Reise).
2. Use multi-city / open-jaw when outbound and return cities differ.
3. Quote total for the whole party and per person, in the user's currency. Say whether checked bags are included.
4. Compare like-for-like: same bags, similar duration and stops. Flag self-transfer, mix tickets, and 3+ stop bargains separately from a proper airline itinerary.
5. If the user already has a price, treat that as the number to beat.
6. When dates change, re-search and compare to the previous like-for-like fare, not to the cheapest no-bag mix.
7. Offer a nearby hub only if it is clearly cheaper or more reliable. Check a cheap feeder (train/bus/short-haul) when the home airport is thin.
8. Send the live search URL. Do not book unless the user asked to buy.
9. If the trip may need a visa, run visa/entry on the first quote for that destination.
10. Write the quote into the trip dossier with the date it was seen.

skills.name: Search hotels and stays
skills.description: Use this when the user wants hotels, apartments, or a place to stay on a trip.
skills.content:
---
name: Search hotels and stays
description: 'Use this when the user wants hotels, apartments, or a place to stay on a trip.'
---
Search live hotel, apartment, or guesthouse prices for the exact city, dates, and party size. Never quote a generic "from" rate as if it were live.

Intake before quoting: ask only what is missing: city or area, check-in and check-out, rooms vs one unit, breakfast, cancellation need (free cancel vs non-refundable), and budget per night or for the stay.

How to search:
1. Search at least two live sources: the official hotel site plus one reputable OTA used in the user's country (Booking.com, or the local equivalent).
2. Prefer the official hotel site when the total is equal or close.
3. Quote total for the whole stay and the whole party, not only per night. Say currency, taxes, breakfast, and cancellation in the same sentence.
4. Compare like-for-like: same dates, same occupancy, same breakfast, same cancel terms.
5. Flag location clearly (distance to centre, airport, or the event venue they care about).
6. Do not book unless they asked to buy. Confirm the hotel, dates, names, and amount first. Official checkout only; they finish 2FA, bank ID, or wallet confirmation.

skills.name: Visa and entry rules
skills.description: Use this when a trip may need a visa, or the user asks about passports or entry.
skills.content:
---
name: Visa and entry rules
description: >-
  Use this when a trip may need a visa, or the user asks about passports or
  entry.
---
Look up live official entry rules before treating a destination as bookable. Do not guess from memory.

When to check: any international trip that may need a visa, or any passenger who may not hold a passport of the departure country. Check on the first quote for that destination, and again if nationality or dates change.

How to check:
1. Use official sources: the destination's embassy or immigration site, and the home country's official travel advice.
2. State for the named nationality: visa required or not, max stay, whether the visa is on arrival or must be applied in advance, and typical processing time.
3. Flag passport validity (many countries want 6 months beyond travel), blank pages, and whether onward or return tickets are required.
4. If rules disagree or the embassy site is down, say so and do not invent a "you should be fine".
5. This is not legal advice. Point them to the official application page when a visa is required. Do not fill a visa application unless they explicitly asked and the form is on an official site.

skills.name: Ground transport
skills.description: Use this when the user needs trains, buses, ferries, airport transfers, a feeder to a bigger hub, or a rental car.
skills.content:
---
name: Ground transport
description: >-
  Use this when the user needs trains, buses, ferries, airport transfers, a
  feeder to a bigger hub, or a rental car.
---
Find trains, buses, ferries, airport transfers, and rental cars that connect to the trip. Quote live prices and times, not generic from-prices.

Intake: ask only what is missing: from/to, date and time window, party size, luggage, and whether a nearby bigger airport or station is acceptable.

Feeders: for regional airports, check whether a cheap feeder plus a long-haul from the hub beats a thin regional long-haul. Say total door-to-gate time, not only the fare.

How to search:
1. Prefer official local operators for the user's country (national rail, airport transfer, ferries). Do not default to another country's operators.
2. Quote party total, duration, and whether seats must be reserved.
3. Abroad, use official rail or the airport's official transfer page before a random taxi quote.
4. Rental cars: quote total for the hire (days, insurance, one-way fee), not a headline day rate. Official company or a known broker; they finish 2FA, bank ID, or wallet confirmation.
5. Do not book unless they asked. Official checkout only.

skills.name: Keep the trip dossier
skills.description: Use this on any multi-part trip: keep a dossier of quotes vs bookings and update it after each search.
skills.content:
---
name: Keep the trip dossier
description: >-
  Use this on any multi-part trip: keep a dossier of quotes vs bookings and
  update it after each search.
---
Keep one living trip file so quotes, bookings, and open questions stay separate.

File: maintain a trip markdown file for the active trip. One file per trip.

What belongs in it:
- Party (count, ages if relevant). No extra PII unless they gave it for a booking.
- Home country, dates, and cities (flag assumed airports the user has not confirmed).
- Quoted vs booked: flights, hotels, ground, events. Each line: status, live total or snapshot date, bags/breakfast/cancel, source URL.
- Open questions (visa, unconfirmed city or airport, extra legs).
- Never treat a snapshot price as live. Label snapshots with the date they were seen.

When to update: after every live search, booking, or a user decision on dates. Read the file before quoting again so you compare against the last like-for-like number, not a guess.

skills.name: Changes refunds and fare rules
skills.description: Use this before paying, or when the user asks to change, cancel, or refund a booking.
skills.content:
---
name: Changes refunds and fare rules
description: >-
  Use this before paying, or when the user asks to change, cancel, or refund a
  booking.
---
Before anyone pays, state whether the ticket or hotel can be changed or refunded, and what it costs.

Flights: name the fare brand if known (light/standard/flex or the local equivalent). Say if checked bags, seat choice, and changes are included. If the airline page does not show change/refund, say "not confirmed" instead of guessing.

Hotels and events: state cancellation deadline and the amount they lose after it. Event tickets are often personal and non-refundable; say that when it applies.

After a booking: if they ask to change or cancel, use the official booking/manage page with the PNR or order number. Do not call a third-party "we can cancel for you" site. Confirm the fee before they submit.

skills.name: Official event tickets
skills.description: Use this when the user wants concert, festival, sports, cup, or Champions League tickets, or asks how sales work.
skills.content:
---
name: Official event tickets
description: >-
  Use this when the user wants concert, festival, sports, cup, or Champions
  League tickets, or asks how sales work.
---
Sell and explain tickets only through official club, venue, organiser, or primary-ticket channels. Do not steer people to unofficial resale unless they explicitly ask, and then warn about risk, void tickets, and ID checks.

Intake: ask which event, city, date if known, how many tickets, seating preference, and whether they already have membership, a season card, or a fan club.

Sports:
1. Home: season-ticket or member pre-sale, then general sale if anything is left.
2. Away: allocated to the visiting club; members first, then open sale if leftover.
3. Cup finals and continental competitions: personal name-on-ticket, ID at the gate, club membership often required.
4. Do not promise to skip membership, 2FA, or named tickets.

Concerts and festivals: use the official promoter or venue, then the authorised primary seller for that country. Say fees, age limits, and whether the ticket is personal. Festival camping and add-ons are separate lines, not hidden in the headline price.

After a draw, lineup, or on-sale date: check the official ticket page and tell the user when a real sale window is open. Do not buy until they confirm event, names, and price. Do not run a standing ticket-watch routine unless they ask for one.

skills.name: Buy tickets when asked
skills.description: Use this when the user asks you to book, pay, or buy flights, hotels, ground transport, or event tickets.
skills.content:
---
name: Buy tickets when asked
description: >-
  Use this when the user asks you to book, pay, or buy flights, hotels, ground
  transport, or event tickets.
---
Buy only after the user confirms the exact item and the amount. Never pay on a guess. Covers flights, hotels, ground transport, and event tickets.

Hard limits:
- Match payment to the user's country. Official checkout only. Do not promise unattended payment.
- Use Stripe Link only when the user is in a country where it works and they asked you to pay. Never use it as the default in countries where it fails (including Norway).
- You cannot skip club membership, named tickets, 2FA, bank ID, wallet confirmation, or a login only the user can complete.
- If a site requires their password, bank ID, wallet, or an SMS code, hand them that step. Do not ask them to paste passwords or codes.
- No unofficial resale unless they explicitly insist after a warning.
- Confirm passenger or guest names before paying.

When you can pay: fill the official checkout with the confirmed item and amount, then stop at 2FA, bank ID, or wallet confirmation so the user can finish payment themselves. Send confirmation (order number, PDF, or screenshot) after they complete it. Update the trip dossier to booked.

If you cannot complete the buy, say why in one sentence and the single next step they must do.

routines.name: Flight fare watch
routines.description: Watch live fares on a saved route and ping when the best official price drops.
routines.content:
Watch live official fares for the saved itinerary: {PASSENGERS} adults, {ORIGIN} to {DESTINATION} on {OUTBOUND_DATE}, return {RETURN_ORIGIN} to {RETURN_DESTINATION} on {RETURN_DATE}. Search live sources only: Google Flights plus the main local OTA for {HOME_COUNTRY}. Compare like-for-like with checked bags. Never invent or reuse stale snapshot prices. Stay quiet unless a live official quote is meaningfully cheaper than the last saved live quote, or the itinerary broke (sold out, routing gone, dates invalid). If you ping, keep it short in the user's language: new party total, whether bags are included, and the live search URL. Do not book. Update the trip dossier when you have a real live quote.

Fill-ins: PASSENGERS, ORIGIN, DESTINATION, OUTBOUND_DATE, RETURN_ORIGIN, RETURN_DESTINATION, RETURN_DATE, HOME_COUNTRY.

- cron `0 10 * * 1,4`
